title: PML Differentially Regulates Growth and Invasion in Brain Cancer.
authors: Tampakaki, Maria; Oraiopoulou, Mariam-Eleni; Tzamali, Eleftheria; Tzedakis, Giorgos; Makatounakis, Takis; Zacharakis, Giannis; Papamatheakis, Joseph; Sakkalis, Vangelis
one_liner_zh: 该文研究PML在胶质母细胞瘤中调控生长与侵袭的作用，属肿瘤细胞生物学与表型模拟，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Glioblastoma is the most malignant brain tumor among adults. Despite multimodality treatment, it remains incurable, mainly because of its extensive heterogeneity and infiltration in the brain parenchyma. Recent evidence indicates dysregulation of the expression of the Promyelocytic Leukemia Protein (PML) in primary Glioblastoma samples. PML is implicated in various ways in cancer biology. In the brain, PML participates in the physiological migration of the neural progenitor cells, which have been hypothesized to serve as the cell of origin of Glioblastoma. The role of PML in Glioblastoma progression has recently gained attention due to its controversial effects in overall Glioblastoma evolution. In this work, we studied the role of PML in Glioblastoma pathophysiology using the U87MG cell line. We genetically modified the cells to conditionally overexpress the PML isoform IV and we focused on its dual role in tumor growth and invasive capacity. Furthermore, we targeted a PML action mediator, the Enhancer of Zeste Homolog 2 (EZH2), via the inhibitory drug DZNeP. We present a combined in vitro-in silico approach, that utilizes both 2D and 3D cultures and cancer-predictive computational algorithms, in order to differentiate and interpret the observed biological results. Our overall findings indicate that PML regulates growth and invasion through distinct cellular mechanisms. In particular, PML overexpression suppresses cell proliferation, while it maintains the invasive capacity of the U87MG Glioblastoma cells and, upon inhibition of the PML-EZH2 pathway, the invasion is drastically eliminated. Our in silico simulations suggest that the underlying mechanism of PML-driven Glioblastoma physiology regulates invasion by differential modulation of the cell-to-cell adhesive and diffusive capacity of the cells. Elucidating further the role of PML in Glioblastoma biology could set PML as a potential molecular biomarker of the tumor progression and its mediated pathway as a therapeutic target, aiming at inhibiting cell growth and potentially clonal evolution regarding their proliferative and/or invasive phenotype within the heterogeneous tumor mass.
abstract_zh: 胶质母细胞瘤是成人中最恶性的脑肿瘤。尽管采用多模式治疗，它仍然无法治愈，主要归因于其在脑实质中的广泛异质性和浸润性。近期证据表明，原发性胶质母细胞瘤样本中早幼粒细胞白血病蛋白（PML）的表达存在失调。PML在癌症生物学中以多种方式参与作用。在大脑中，PML参与神经祖细胞的生理性迁移，而这些细胞被假设为胶质母细胞瘤的起源细胞。PML在胶质母细胞瘤进展中的作用因其对整体胶质母细胞瘤演化的争议性影响而近期受到关注。在本研究中，我们利用U87MG细胞系探讨了PML在胶质母细胞瘤病理生理学中的作用。我们通过基因修饰使细胞条件性过表达PML异构体IV，并聚焦于其在肿瘤生长和侵袭能力中的双重作用。此外，我们通过抑制性药物DZNeP靶向了PML作用介导因子——Zeste同源物增强子2（EZH2）。我们采用了一种结合体外与计算机模拟的方法，利用二维和三维培养以及癌症预测计算算法，以区分并解释观察到的生物学结果。我们的总体发现表明，PML通过不同的细胞机制调控生长和侵袭。具体而言，PML过表达抑制细胞增殖，同时维持U87MG胶质母细胞瘤细胞的侵袭能力，并且在抑制PML-EZH2通路后，侵袭能力被显著消除。我们的计算机模拟表明，PML驱动的胶质母细胞瘤生理学的基础机制通过差异调节细胞间粘附能力和扩散能力来调控侵袭。进一步阐明PML在胶质母细胞瘤生物学中的作用，可能将PML确立为肿瘤进展的潜在分子生物标志物，并将其介导的通路作为治疗靶点，旨在抑制细胞生长及潜在克隆演化，涉及异质性肿瘤团块内的增殖和/或侵袭表型。
